introduction: This roadmap is designed to guide aspiring programmers through a comprehensive journey of learning Python, from foundational concepts to advanced topics and practical application. It emphasizes a hands-on approach, combining theoretical knowledge with practical exercises and projects to build strong programming skills. Each stage builds upon the previous one, ensuring a logical and progressive learning experience.

stages.title: Stage 1: Python Fundamentals & Setup
stages.description: This stage covers the absolute basics of Python programming, including setting up your development environment, understanding core syntax, variables, data types, and basic control flow. It's the essential foundation for all subsequent learning.

items.name: 1.1 Introduction to Python & Environment Setup
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Understand what Python is used for, install Python, set up a development environment (IDE/text editor), and run your first 'Hello World' program.
Prerequisites: Basic computer literacy.
Time Commitment: 4-6 hours
Difficulty: Easy
Practical Exercise: Install Python and VS Code (or preferred IDE), write and run 'Hello World'.
resources: Real Python: How to Install Python

items.name: 1.2 Variables, Data Types & Operators
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Define and use variables, understand fundamental data types (integers, floats, strings, booleans), and apply arithmetic, comparison, and logical operators.
Prerequisites: Stage 1.1
Time Commitment: 6-8 hours
Difficulty: Easy
Practical Exercise: Write a script that calculates the area of a rectangle given length and width, and prints the result. Experiment with different data types and operators.
resources: Corey Schafer: Python Tutorial for Beginners - Variables, Strings, and Numbers

items.name: 1.3 Basic Input/Output & Type Conversion
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Take user input using input(), display output using print(), and convert between different data types (e.g., string to int).
Prerequisites: Stage 1.2
Time Commitment: 3-4 hours
Difficulty: Easy
Practical Exercise: Create a program that asks the user for their name and age, then prints a greeting message including their age in 5 years.
resources: Python Official Docs: Input and Output

items.name: 1.4 Conditional Statements (if/elif/else)
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Implement decision-making logic using if, elif, and else statements. Understand indentation and logical flow.
Prerequisites: Stage 1.3
Time Commitment: 5-7 hours
Difficulty: Easy
Project: Simple Grade Calculator - Ask the user for a score (0-100) and print the corresponding letter grade (A, B, C, D, F).

stages.title: Stage 2: Core Data Structures & Control Flow
stages.description: This stage delves into Python's fundamental data structures for organizing data and introduces more advanced control flow mechanisms like loops and functions, which are crucial for writing reusable and efficient code.

items.name: 2.1 Lists & Tuples
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Create, manipulate, and iterate over lists and tuples. Understand their differences and when to use each.
Prerequisites: Stage 1.4
Time Commitment: 7-9 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Practical Exercise: Create a list of your favorite movies. Add a new movie, remove an old one, and print the list in alphabetical order. Create a tuple of coordinates and access elements.
resources: Real Python: Python Lists and Tuples

items.name: 2.2 Dictionaries & Sets
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Create, manipulate, and iterate over dictionaries (key-value pairs) and sets (unique elements). Understand their use cases.
Prerequisites: Stage 2.1
Time Commitment: 7-9 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Practical Exercise: Create a dictionary representing a person's profile (name, age, city). Add a new key-value pair, update an existing one, and iterate through keys and values. Create a set of numbers and perform set operations (union, intersection).

items.name: 2.3 Loops (for & while)
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Use for loops to iterate over sequences and while loops for conditional repetition. Understand break and continue statements.
Prerequisites: Stage 2.2
Time Commitment: 6-8 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Practical Exercise: Write a for loop to print all even numbers from 1 to 20. Write a while loop that asks the user for input until they type 'quit'.

items.name: 2.4 Functions
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Define and call functions, pass arguments, return values, understand scope (local vs. global variables), and use default arguments and keyword arguments.
Prerequisites: Stage 2.3
Time Commitment: 8-10 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Project: To-Do List Manager - Create functions to add tasks, view tasks, mark tasks as complete, and delete tasks from a list. Use loops and conditionals to build a menu-driven interface.
resources: Corey Schafer: Python Tutorial for Beginners - Functions

stages.title: Stage 3: Modularity, Error Handling & File I/O
stages.description: This stage focuses on making your code more organized, robust, and capable of interacting with external data sources. You'll learn how to structure larger projects, handle unexpected issues, and read/write files.

items.name: 3.1 Modules & Packages
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Create and import custom modules, understand how to organize code into packages, and use built-in modules (e.g., math, random).
Prerequisites: Stage 2.4
Time Commitment: 5-7 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Practical Exercise: Create a module with several mathematical functions (e.g., add, subtract, multiply). Import and use these functions in a separate script. Experiment with from ... import ....
resources: Real Python: Python Modules and Packages

items.name: 3.2 Error and Exception Handling
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Understand different types of errors, use try, except, else, and finally blocks to handle exceptions gracefully, and raise custom exceptions.
Prerequisites: Stage 3.1
Time Commitment: 6-8 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Practical Exercise: Write a program that asks for two numbers and performs division. Implement try-except to handle ValueError (non-numeric input) and ZeroDivisionError.
resources: Python Official Docs: Errors and Exceptions

items.name: 3.3 File Input/Output (I/O)
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Open, read from, and write to text files. Understand different file modes ('r', 'w', 'a'). Use with statements for automatic file closing.
Prerequisites: Stage 3.2
Time Commitment: 7-9 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Project: Simple Contact Book - Create a program that allows users to add new contacts (name, phone, email) to a text file, view all contacts, and search for a contact. Store each contact on a new line in the file.
resources: Python Official Docs: Reading and Writing Files
Real Python: Reading and Writing Files in Python

stages.title: Stage 4: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)
stages.description: This stage introduces the powerful paradigm of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), which is essential for building complex, maintainable, and scalable applications. You'll learn to model real-world entities using classes and objects.

items.name: 4.1 Classes & Objects
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Define classes, create objects (instances), understand attributes (data) and methods (behavior), and use the __init__ constructor.
Prerequisites: Stage 3.3
Time Commitment: 8-10 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Practical Exercise: Create a Dog class with attributes like name, breed, age, and methods like bark() and sit(). Create multiple Dog objects and call their methods.
resources: Corey Schafer: Python Tutorial for Beginners - OOP

items.name: 4.2 Inheritance & Polymorphism
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Understand inheritance for code reuse, create subclasses, override methods, and grasp the concept of polymorphism (different objects responding to the same method call).
Prerequisites: Stage 4.1
Time Commitment: 7-9 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Practical Exercise: Extend the Dog class to create a GoldenRetriever subclass. Add a specific method for GoldenRetriever. Create a generic Animal class and demonstrate polymorphism with different animal types.

items.name: 4.3 Encapsulation & Abstraction (Properties, Dunder Methods)
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Understand encapsulation through private/protected attributes (convention), use properties (@property decorator) for controlled access, and explore common 'dunder' (double underscore) methods like __str__, __repr__.
Prerequisites: Stage 4.2
Time Commitment: 6-8 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Project: Basic RPG Game - Design classes for Player, Enemy, Weapon, Armor. Implement attributes and methods for health, attack, defense. Use inheritance for different enemy types. Demonstrate __str__ for object representation.
resources: Python Official Docs: Data Model (Special Method Names)

stages.title: Stage 5: Advanced Topics & Standard Libraries
stages.description: This stage introduces more advanced Python features that enable more elegant and efficient code, along with exploring powerful capabilities provided by Python's extensive standard library and popular third-party modules.

items.name: 5.1 Generators & Decorators
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Understand and implement generators for memory-efficient iteration, and use decorators to modify function behavior without changing their source code.
Prerequisites: Stage 4.3
Time Commitment: 8-10 hours
Difficulty: Hard
Practical Exercise: Create a generator function for an infinite sequence (e.g., Fibonacci numbers). Write a decorator that logs the execution time of any function.
resources: Python Official Docs: Iterators and Generators

items.name: 5.2 Context Managers (with statement)
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Understand the purpose of context managers for resource management, and implement custom context managers using classes or the contextlib module.
Prerequisites: Stage 5.1
Time Commitment: 4-6 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Practical Exercise: Create a custom context manager that prints 'Entering context' and 'Exiting context' when used with a with statement.
resources: Python Official Docs: With Statement Context Managers

items.name: 5.3 Working with Standard Libraries (os, sys, datetime, math, json)
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Utilize common modules from Python's standard library for tasks like interacting with the operating system (os, sys), handling dates and times (datetime), performing mathematical operations (math), and working with JSON data (json).
Prerequisites: Stage 5.2
Time Commitment: 10-12 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Project: Directory Organizer - Write a script that scans a specified directory, identifies files by extension, and moves them into organized subdirectories (e.g., 'Images', 'Documents'). Use os module functions.

items.name: 5.4 Introduction to Third-Party Libraries (e.g., requests, pandas, numpy)
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Understand how to install and use third-party libraries using pip. Get a brief overview of popular libraries like requests (HTTP), pandas (data analysis), numpy (numerical computing), and BeautifulSoup (web scraping).
Prerequisites: Stage 5.3
Time Commitment: 8-10 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Project: Simple Web Scraper - Use requests to fetch content from a public website (e.g., a news site) and BeautifulSoup to parse the HTML and extract headlines or specific data points. (Focus on a simple, ethical scrape).

stages.title: Stage 6: Practical Application & Project Development
stages.description: This final stage focuses on consolidating knowledge through larger projects, introducing best practices for collaborative development, and exploring pathways into specific domains like web development or data science.

items.name: 6.1 Version Control with Git & GitHub
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Understand the basics of version control, initialize Git repositories, commit changes, branch, merge, and push code to GitHub.
Prerequisites: Stage 5.4
Time Commitment: 10-12 hours
Difficulty: Medium
Practical Exercise: Create a GitHub account, initialize a local Git repository for one of your previous projects, commit changes, and push it to a new remote repository on GitHub. Practice branching and merging.

items.name: 6.2 Virtual Environments
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Understand why virtual environments are important, create and activate virtual environments, and manage project dependencies using pip and requirements.txt.
Prerequisites: Stage 6.1
Time Commitment: 3-5 hours
Difficulty: Easy
Practical Exercise: For a new project, create a virtual environment, install a third-party library (e.g., requests), and generate a requirements.txt file.

items.name: 6.3 Introduction to a Python Framework/Domain
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Get an introductory understanding of a specific Python domain. Choose ONE of the following paths:
    A) Web Development (e.g., Flask/Django): Understand basic web concepts, create a simple 'Hello World' web app.
    B) Data Science (e.g., Pandas/Numpy): Perform basic data loading, cleaning, and analysis.
    C) GUI Development (e.g., Tkinter/PyQt): Build a simple desktop application with buttons and text fields.
    D) Automation/Scripting: Develop a more complex automation script (e.g., email sender, file processor).
Prerequisites: Stage 6.2
Time Commitment: 15-20 hours
Difficulty: Medium to Hard (depending on chosen domain)
Practical Exercise: Follow a beginner tutorial for your chosen framework/domain to build a small, functional application.

items.name: 6.4 Final Capstone Project
items.description:
Learning Outcomes: Apply all learned concepts to build a significant project from scratch. This project should integrate multiple Python features, potentially use external libraries, and demonstrate problem-solving skills.
Prerequisites: Stage 6.3
Time Commitment: 20-40 hours (flexible)
Difficulty: Hard
Project: Choose a project aligned with your interests and the domain explored in 6.3. Examples: A simple blog web application, a data analysis tool for a public dataset, a desktop calculator, a command-line utility for managing notes, a game with a GUI. Plan, design, implement, and document your project. Use Git for version control.
resources: Project-based learning platforms (e.g., freeCodeCamp, Codecademy projects)
